Data are observations of the real world; models are abstractions of it. Good data science connects the two through careful measurement, rigorous modelling, and thoughtful presentation and interpretation.

## How I work

From how the data were generated to the decisions they support. Each step starts from a problem I've seen in scientific data work.

::: {.pipeline}

::: {.step}
[Measure]{.step-label}

[“This result looks wrong, and nobody can say why.”]{.step-problem}

Start with how the data were generated: instruments, detection limits, and sampling design.

[For example]{.step-eg} [MSc research in analytical toxicology](scientific-communication.qmd){.step-link}
:::

::: {.step}
[Engineer]{.step-label}

[“We rebuild the same analysis by hand every year.”]{.step-problem}

Turn messy, multi-source data into reproducible, tested pipelines with built-in QA/QC checks.

[For example]{.step-eg} [Water Quality Harmonization](projects/wq-harmonization/index.qmd){.step-link}
:::

::: {.step}
[Model]{.step-label}

[“We’ve collected years of data and only run the standard test.”]{.step-problem}

Match the model to the pattern in the data and check its assumptions before trusting the result.

[For example]{.step-eg} [Modelling Beyond a Straight Line](projects/vignette-non-linear-trends/index.qmd){.step-link}
:::

::: {.step}
[Deploy]{.step-label}

[“The results live in a PDF or on one person’s laptop.”]{.step-problem}

Build reports, dashboards, and apps that people can use without opening the code.

[For example]{.step-eg} [IBD Mycobiome Dashboard](projects/ibd-mycobiome-dashboard/index.qmd){.step-link}
:::

::: {.step}
[Decide]{.step-label}

[“Will this hold up to review?”]{.step-problem}

Document steps; create reproducible environments; communicate results clearly enough to support decisions.

[For example]{.step-eg} [Six years of consulting](resume.qmd#experience){.step-link}
:::

:::
